The US added just 29,000 jobs in September. Wall Street expected 84,000.

Wage growth has slowed to 3.0% year over year, down from north of 4%. July was revised into the red, and healthcare was almost the entire gain at 17,000 jobs.

This is a labor market downshifting, not overheating. Softer wages kill the inflation-scare and flag slowing growth instead. The case for rate cuts just got louder, and the front end of the curve moves first.

tweets.text:
The Atlantic just broke a century-old record. This deep into the season, it has had zero hurricanes.

By now the North Atlantic normally has more than three. This year, none. Eight named storms formed, but every one got torn apart within days.

The culprit is El Niño. Warm air rising off the Pacific is generating high-altitude winds that blow east across the Atlantic and shred storms before they can organize. Forecasters call it vertical wind shear, and it is running well above normal right where hurricanes are born.

Two market reads. Gulf energy caught a break, with no refinery or platform shutdowns in an already tight fuel market. And property-catastrophe insurers and reinsurers are looking at one of their calmest seasons on record, which means fewer claims and fatter underwriting margins.

A hurricane-free season is a gift to the cat-exposed insurers. That is where it shows up in the numbers.

Private equity has a problem. Wall Street has a fix: your 401k.

PE funds are sitting on trillions of dollars of companies they bought years ago and still cannot sell. Deal activity keeps falling, and the deals that do happen take longer and longer to close. The industry is gummed up.

So regulators just proposed opening private funds to everyday investors and retirement accounts. Read that again. The moment institutions stop buying what these funds are holding, the plan is to sell it to you.

These funds are illiquid, charge 2 and 20, and are hard to value. You may not get your money out when you need it. A pension can lock capital up for decades. You cannot. And the sponsor stocks themselves are down 12% to 36% this year.

When Wall Street is this eager to hand retail what institutions are backing away from, hold onto your wallet.

tweets.text: Our Strategy product is unique in that we deemphasize market and sector calls, instead translating our market and macro views into sector-neutral long portfolios that are measured against a relevant benchmark. Our R1k Tech portfolio has *outperformed* by ~35% this year versus the equal-weighted Tech sector. We purposely measure against EW b/c our goal is to provide clients a basket of stocks with high “hit” rates (strong breadth). Performance doesn’t include trading costs, and can be implemented through various trading vehicles (swaps/baskets, etc). We update the basket with full transparency, allowing us to “grade” our investment recommendations throughout the year(s). I’ve focused less on sectors in recent years as concentration has made such calls more idiosyncratic and less “macro.” The factors we’ve emphasized year to date have been Value (P/E), fundamental momentum (EPS revisions & EPS Surprise) and profitability (ROE). The recipe changes as the outlook, the cycle, and sentiment evolves. We’ve captured a large share of the AI outperformers through targeting these fundamental attributes. No stories, just numbers. We’ve been running these portfolios since 2018 because I got tired of clients asking me what my calls (market, sector) were in the past and not having a systematic way to answer - these portfolios are all on our client portal for them to see. Currently there are 18 stocks in this basket.
